clue.text: Sword-swallower is not one to strike a minstrel

parts.note: a scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike
a bard is a minstrel or poet

explanation.surface: A fire-eater type who won't join the picket line and hits a wandering singer instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sword-swallower' sounds like a circus act, but it is the sheath that swallows the blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath takes in the whole blade, so it playfully 'swallows' the weapon.

clue.text: The companion I love in Rome is a wild creature

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
amo is Latin, the language of Rome, for 'I love'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's friend declares their love in the Eternal City, and turns out to be a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The chamois is a goat-antelope living wild in European mountains.

clue.text: He serves little Arthur during, drinking bout

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bender is a heavy drinking session
Art is the short form of the name Arthur

explanation.surface: A man pours drinks for young Arthur in the middle of a binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He serves' could be a waiter or tennis player; 'during' signals that one piece sits inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman's job is to serve customers drinks.

clue.text: Gaoled drunken ancient

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A jailed old man who was drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges the letters of GAOLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has existed for ages is very old, i.e. ancient.

clue.text: His turn came when he was summoned by bells

definitions.text: His turn came when he was summoned by bells

parts.words: His turn came when he was summoned by bells
parts.note: in the legend, the London bells called 'Turn again' to a boy leaving the city, who returned to become Lord Mayor

explanation.surface: Someone waiting for their go until a bell rings for them.
explanation.walkthrough: The story: a poor boy leaving London heard Bow Bells chime 'Turn again', went back and became Lord Mayor three times; it is a favourite British pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Lord Mayor turned back to London on hearing the bells.

clue.text: Soldier enters, holding back Galatea as an example

indicators.note: back says the held letters are read from right to left
the two words hold the needed letters within them, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A soldier comes in carrying back a statue-woman as a sample.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' takes DIEREN from 'solDIER ENters'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Galatea was one of the sea nymphs, daughters of Nereus.

clue.text: No Scots capture posh country mansion in revolt

indicators.note: the first piece captures the others, holding them inside

parts.note: nae is the Scots word for no
U means upper-class, posh
a country seat is a grand house on an estate

explanation.surface: Scottish rebels refuse to seize a stately home during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolt' looks like a noun for an uprising but is the verb meaning disgust; 'capture' signals one piece holding the others.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt someone is to disgust them, making them feel sick.

clue.text: The last judgement — record it on Herbert

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
taken as written
A. P. Herbert was a British humorist and MP, known by his initials APH

explanation.surface: A biblical day of reckoning noted down on a man called Herbert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last judgement' suggests Doomsday, but it is the final verdict carved on a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Words on a tombstone are a final appraisal of the dead person.

clue.text: Canine check

explanation.surface: A vet examining a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's fang is literally a canine; the same name is given to a jagged checked cloth pattern.

clue.text: Visionary sort of fire grips Irish poet

indicators.note: the anagram grips the poet, holding him inside
sort of means a version of, so the letters of fire are rearranged

parts.note: AE was the pen name of the Irish poet George William Russell

explanation.surface: A kind of blaze surrounds a poet from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' turns FIRE into FRIE, which 'grips' AE: F + AE + RIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Faerie is fairyland, a realm of imagined, dreamlike enchantment.

clue.text: Running about following game

definitions.meaning: chasing quarry, as in hare hunting with greyhounds

explanation.surface: A child dashing about after a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Water coursing flows swiftly; hare coursing is the sport of hounds chasing hares by sight.

clue.text: Firm rule about the French salad

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a law is a rule
les is the French plural for 'the'

explanation.surface: A company regulation concerning French matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals one piece going round another; COLE-SLAW is split here unusually as a hyphenated (4-4) entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredded cabbage in mayonnaise is a common salad side dish.

clue.text: Optical instrument with head missing but still going

indicators.note: the instrument's head is its first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a sextant is an optical device for measuring angles in navigation

explanation.surface: A broken telescope with its top gone still works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with head missing' takes S off SEXTANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extant still survives, as with documents that remain in existence.

clue.text: It's inaudible to the other players in a team

definitions.text: It's inaudible to the other players

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A whisper on the pitch that the opposing players cannot hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' suggests sport, but these are actors: a stage remark the rest of the cast pretend not to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre a remark spoken to the audience is unheard by the other characters.

clue.text: Collect material for concrete

definitions.meaning: the crushed stone or gravel mixed with cement

explanation.surface: Gathering supplies for a building job.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather into a total is to amass; the gravel bound by cement in concrete has the same name.

clue.text: The Colonel, it's said, has one topic in mess

indicators.note: in a mess means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An army colonel brings up a single subject in the officers' mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonel' is said like 'kernel', and this green nut is a kernel. 'in mess' rearranges HAS + I + TOPIC; the mess sounds military but is the anagram sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel sounds like kernel, the edible inside of a nut such as this.

clue.text: It's not alphabetical, that's obvious of course

parts.note: something clear is obvious
soup is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: Something that isn't in A-to-Z order, and that's plain, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Alphabet soup has pasta letters in it; a consommé has none, so it is 'not alphabetical'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain broth with no pasta letters is the opposite of alphabet soup.

clue.text: Having just married Wendy, we left to change

indicators.note: the letters are made to change their order

explanation.surface: A couple recently wed to Wendy decide to move on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges WENDY + WE + L.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone recently wed has only just tied the knot.

clue.text: Cloth for man at the pottery.. centre

parts.note: George is a man's name

indicators.note: the centre of the word pottery is its middle letters

explanation.surface: Fabric for a worker in a ceramics studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes the middle three letters TTE from poTTEry.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgette is a thin, sheer crêpe fabric.

clue.text: Perhaps prove to be superior

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Maybe demonstrating that you are better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges PROVE + TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise above or surpass something is to be higher than it.

clue.text: Everyone is after soft fruit

indicators.note: is after means the one piece follows the other in the answer

parts.note: p (piano) means soft in music
each means every one

explanation.surface: Everybody is chasing soft fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft fruit' looks like the definition, but soft is P.
explanation.definitionFit: The peach is a stone fruit with velvety skin.

clue.text: One of the toasts that may be offered with 15

definitions.text: One of the toasts that may be offered with 15

parts.words: One of the toasts that may be offered with 15
parts.note: the toasts are not drinks to someone's health but small cubes of fried bread served in soup

explanation.surface: A drink raised to someone at a dinner where broth is served.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cube of fried or toasted bread is served floating in soup.

clue.text: Come to stir

explanation.surface: Wake up and move.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse from sleep is both to regain consciousness and to start moving.

clue.text: An attractive woman — this much one can see

definitions.meaning: as much as the eyes take in at once

explanation.surface: A beauty who is quite a sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunning person is slang for something good to look at; literally it is as much as one look takes in.

clue.text: The place for pressmen — or womens movement?

indicators.note: movement means the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Journalists' office, or perhaps the women's liberation movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like the women's movement but rearranges OR + WOMENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists work in the office where a paper's news is gathered.

clue.text: Refined salt suitable for a high-up?

definitions.meaning: Attic salt is classical term for elegant, pointed humour
humorously, cleverness kept in a loft

explanation.surface: Purified salt, fit for a VIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic (Athenian) wit was refined humour; an attic is the top room of a house, high up.

clue.text: Like a cat's cradle, hard to explain

definitions.meaning: full of tangles, as the string game is

explanation.surface: The string game is a puzzle to describe.
explanation.definitionFit: The string game is all loops and tangles; a tangled problem is difficult to solve.

clue.text: Caught sight of French art, particoloured

parts.note: es is French for 'art' as in 'thou art' (tu es)
pied means patched in two or more colours

explanation.surface: Glimpsed a multicoloured piece of French painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' here is the old verb 'thou art', not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to spot or notice something.

clue.text: They don't usually stand up to the cheese

definitions.text: They don't usually stand up to the cheese

parts.words: They don't usually stand up to the cheese
parts.note: in skittles the cheese is the heavy disc thrown at the pins, which usually knocks them down

explanation.surface: People who cannot cope with a cheese course.
explanation.walkthrough: In British skittles, the 'cheese' is the flat wooden disc thrown at the pins.
explanation.definitionFit: The pins in skittles are set up and toppled by the thrown disc.
